title: example-user and ZimaOS: Building a Retro LAN Party Server
meta_title: example-user’s ZimaOS Retro LAN Party Server Story
meta_description: Meet example-user, a DIY hobbyist who used ZimaOS as a lightweight Unraid alternative for a retro LAN party server with Docker, VMs, DNS, and TeamSpeak.

community_source.title: Zima User Story Questionnaire — example-user
community_source.excerpt: A February 2026 creator questionnaire describing a ZimaOS retro LAN-party server running two Docker containers and three VMs on reused desktop hardware.

html:
A Note from Zima

Thank you, example-user, for showing that a useful home server does not have to begin with purpose-built server hardware.

— Zima

Meet example-user

example-user describes himself as a non-professional technology user and DIY hobbyist.

A Retro LAN Party Became the Test Case

By the time he documented the build, ZimaOS was already running two Docker containers: a TeamSpeak server and a DNS server.

Why ZimaOS Worked as a Lightweight Unraid Alternative

example-user's comparison with Unraid was deliberately practical.

Once the Hardware Settled Down, the Server Stayed Stable

After reducing the network-card count, example-user reported that the system ran steadily.

A Non-Professional User's Definition of Success

What makes this project useful is that example-user did not judge the system by how many advanced features it exposed.

The Story Is Still Being Written

For current platform context, see the ZimaOS feature overview and the current RAID configuration reference.
